newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Alpha raises A$22.7 mln to fund acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Alpha raises A$22.7 mln to fund acquisition.

text.p: Alpha Healthcare Ltd said on Wednesday it planned to raise A$22.7 million through the issue of shares and convertible notes to fund a A$38 million acquisition of Health Care Corporation Pty Ltd.

Alpha said the acquisiton of Health Care Corp, a New South Wales private hospital operator, in a structured acquisition from Health Care Corp owners James Hardie Industries Ltd and Leighton Holdings LTd.
Alpha managing director Paul Hopper said in a statement the transaction was a major step in Alpha's strategy of building a significant presence as an integrated healthcare provider.

The transaction would be funded through a mixture of equity and debt. Alpha would raise A$18.7 million by the issue of 103.8 million 20 cent ordinary shares issued partly paid to 18 cents which would, subject to shareholder approval, be paid up to 20 cents from the share premium account.
Of this equity A$15 million would be provided by Sun Healthcare Group Inc of the United States.

A further A$4 million would be raised by the issue of unsecured convertible notes which would mature five years from the date of issue or be convertible in Alpha ordinary fully paid 20 ceents shares at 30 cents per share.
Alpha said Sun Healthcare, based in Albuquerque, New Mexico, is the third largest provider of contract rehabilitation, the sixth largest nursing home operator.

Alpha's purchase includes the rights to the Westmead Private Hospital project, a tertiary care 136-bed hospital, which is expected to cost around A$44 million and to be operational at the end of calendar 1999.

Hopper said Alpha Healthcare would continue to pursue opportunities for growth and possible realignments of other health groups, as well as privatisation and co-location of state and federal hospital services.
"Alpha is on track to increase profits and earnings per share in the current financial year," he said.
